name: Tiered Plant Stand
pitch: A stepped plant stand cut to your window or wall: 2 to 4 slatted shelves, raised for the robot vacuum, with an anti-tip anchor.

stages.title: Cut the sheet
stages.detail: Run the fit-test coupon (slot = tab + 0.1 mm), then cut 1 sheet from the DXF (CUT layer): 35 m of path, 68 drainage slots. Inside-out order, air assist on. If the ply is exterior/marine grade, expect the phenolic glue lines to char more: slow down and test a scrap.

stages.title: Remove char and sand
stages.detail: Brush char from every edge, 120 then 180 grit; ease the shelf edges. Sand the drainage slots with a folded strip of paper.

stages.title: Dry fit
stages.detail: Lay SIDE-L flat, push the 3 SHELF boards and the two rails into its slots, add SIDE-R. Check each shelf tab ends flush with the outside face and the stair profile lines up. No glue.

stages.title: Pre-finish
stages.detail: Seal every face and edge now: 3 coats of spar urethane or exterior poly (wet pots, spills). Mask tabs and slots so the glue still bonds. Seal the drainage slot edges well; they take the water.

stages.title: Glue-up (Titebond III, water-resistant)
stages.detail: Glue the 3 shelf tabs and the two rail tabs into SIDE-L, then fit SIDE-R and clamp across the width. Wipe squeeze-out at once; check square by measuring both diagonals.

stages.title: Screws as clamps
stages.detail: 10 #8 screws (3.0 mm pilots pre-cut): #8 x 1-1/2 in through the side faces into the shelf edges, between the tabs. Use coated or stainless screws if it will live outdoors.

stages.title: Anti-tip anchor
stages.detail: Fit the anti-tip strap through one of the two 6 mm holes in RAIL-TOP into a wall stud. Heavy pots on the top tier raise the tipping risk, so keep the heaviest pots on the bottom tier.

stages.title: Final coat, cure, pack
stages.detail: Last coat on the top faces, 24 h cure, 15 kg pot load test on each shelf, felt/rubber pads on the 4 feet, flat-pack in one box (about 720 x 820 x 80 mm).

materials.sheet: 18 mm (3/4 in) birch or Baltic-birch plywood, 4 x 8 ft (1220 x 2440 mm) x 1; use exterior-grade ply for a patio stand
materials.finish: spar urethane or exterior poly, 3 coats (about $14)

safety: Anchor to a wall stud with the anti-tip strap (ASTM F3096 style); mandatory above 900 mm, recommended on every unit.
Rated target 15 kg per shelf (UNVERIFIED - load test a shelf before selling). Wet soil is heavy: 5 L of damp potting mix is about 4 kg.
Not a children's product (no CPSIA testing). Not a climbing aid.
Outdoor use needs exterior-grade ply plus a UV-rated finish; indoor-grade birch ply swells and delaminates when wet.

profit.labels: ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS ONLY - not quotes, not guaranteed, machine time NOT measured on the real machine
profit.assumptions: All dollar figures are planning ESTIMATES / ASSUMPTIONS, not quotes, not guaranteed. Sheet prices: 4x8 ft 18 mm birch plywood $70-110, basic plywood $55-75 (assumption). Machine time uses a sourced RANGE for a 120 W diode on 18 mm ply (low 120 / typical 300 / high 600 mm/min effective, i.e. after multiple passes; see CUT-SPEED-RESEARCH.md); ACMER publishes no 18 mm ply feed rate, so none of it is measured on this machine. Machine wear/electricity $1.70 per machine-hour (assumption). Labor valued at $25/h for the "after labor" line only. Marketplace fees 10% (assumption, e.g. Etsy-style).

machine_time.label: ESTIMATE. Diode = ACMER X1 Ultra 120 W on 18 mm plywood; effective rate = speed / passes. Includes rapid travel between contours and 15 min per sheet of load/focus/unload. Not measured.

commercial_laser.label: ASSUMPTION. Sourced case: 300-600 W CO2 flatbed, single pass at ~600 mm/min (vendor 480-720), 60 m/min rapids, 5 min/sheet, $8/h operating cost. What-if cases: a machine 10x / 20x faster than the diode mid cut+travel time (not sourced for 18 mm ply).

profit.price_band_source: My estimate: Etsy/Amazon plywood plant stands run about $30-$110 for small units (SHORTLIST.md R1, third-party estimates); a window- or wall-fitted 3-tier unit with slatted shelves, finished, is priced above that. Low = 2-tier unfinished, high = 4-tier finished and sized to order.
profit.note_machine_time: ESTIMATE: 2.3 h (low-speed case 5.2 h, best case 1.3 h) of machine time per unit for 35 m of cut path in 1 sheet(s) on a 120 W diode, 18 mm plywood. Machine time, not material, is still the limit on profit per hour, but a single test cut on scrap will replace this range with a real number.

unverified: Machine time is an estimate (120 W diode on 18 mm ply, sourced range, not measured on this machine); cut time and profit/hour depend on it.
Shelf load rating and deflection untested; the deflection line in checks.txt is a hand calculation with an assumed ply modulus.
Exterior/marine ply (phenolic glue) cut quality on the diode laser is unverified.

The cost model charges one whole 4x8 sheet but this design fills only 34% of it (offcut not credited). Nesting 2 stands per sheet (area allows it; not nested here) would cut mid cost to about $83 and lift mid gross margin from 22% to about 49%. As modeled, the low price band is below cost.
Price band is my estimate, not a market quote.
